# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

I am Deaf. I see the bomb: Display shows 0, Light is red, and there are three wires (Red, Yellow, Green). I cannot hear anyone.

Blind has just gestured to me: [👋 👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟].
I need to interpret this. Since Blind is blind, they likely know their own position or role relative to the wires, or perhaps they are trying to communicate a sequence based on touch. However, without a shared code established in Turn 1, these gestures are ambiguous. "👋" might mean hello/stop. "👉" points right? "☝" one finger up. "✌" two fingers. "🤟" love sign (ILY)?

Crucially, I need to communicate what I *see* to Mute and Blind so they can help.
Mute can read the manual but cannot speak or touch.
Blind can touch the bomb but cannot see.

If I speak, both Mute and Blind receive it (since speech carries words). Wait, the rules say: "Whoever can hear receives your words".
- Deaf (Me): Cannot hear.
- Mute: Can hear? The table says Mute "Cannot Speak". It doesn't explicitly say Mute cannot hear. Usually, Mute implies inability to speak, not hear. Let's assume Mute can hear.
- Blind: Can hear? The table says Blind "Can Reach... Cannot See". It doesn't say cannot hear. Usually, Blind implies inability to see, not hear. So Blind can hear.

So if I `speak`, both Mute and Blind should receive the text. This is efficient.

What do I tell them?
1. The current state: Display 0, Light Red, Wires R/Y/G.
2. My interpretation of Blind's gesture: I don't know it yet. I should ask for clarification or describe my view clearly so they can correlate.

However, Blind gestured *to me*. Did Mute see it? No, Mute reads the manual, doesn't necessarily see the room/bomb unless specified. The prompt says Mute "Reads the manual". It doesn't say Mute sees the bomb. Deaf "Sees the bomb". Blind "Feels the bomb".
So Mute probably does *not* see the bomb or the gestures directly. Mute only knows the manual.
Blind feels the bomb.
Deaf sees the bomb.

Therefore:
- I must tell Mute what I see so Mute can look up the procedure in the manual.
- I must tell Blind what I see so Blind can verify tactile features against visual ones (e.g., "is there a button here?").

Blind's gesture [👋 👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟] was directed at me. If Mute can't see it, I need to relay it or ignore it until I understand it. But since I don't understand it, I should focus on establishing the baseline facts from my view.

Let's describe the bomb precisely.
"Display 0. Light Red. Three wires: Left Red, Middle Yellow, Right Green."

This gives Mute the info to check the manual.
This gives Blind the info to confirm wire positions/colors by touch (if colors are distinguishable by texture or if they are labeled).

I will speak to everyone (default) because both Mute and Blind likely have hearing.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is red. There are three wires: left is red, middle is yellow, right is green.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈]

I see the bomb state remains unchanged: Display 0, Light Red, Wires Red/Yellow/Green.
Mute has gestured to me with a single symbol: 👈 (pointing left).

Since I am Deaf, I cannot hear any speech Mute might have made (though Mute is mute by definition, so they can't speak anyway). I rely on gestures from Mute and Blind.
Blind previously gestured [👋 👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟].
Mute now gestures [👈].

I need to interpret these.
If 👈 means "left" or "wire 1", it aligns with my visual observation that Wire 1 is Red.
However, without a established code, I must be careful.
The most useful thing I can do is provide clear textual descriptions of what I see to Blind (who can hear) and ensure Mute knows I've received their gesture if possible, but I can't gesture back to Mute effectively if they don't see? No, Mute sees gestures. I can gesture to Mute.

Let's assume standard directional meanings for now or try to establish a baseline.
Wire 1 is Left. Wire 2 is Middle. Wire 3 is Right.
Mute pointing Left likely refers to Wire 1.

I should confirm the wire colors to Blind again, perhaps emphasizing the order, and maybe gesture back to Mute to acknowledge receipt or ask for clarification. But since I don't know the manual, I can't make decisions. I just report.

Wait, looking at the previous turn, I spoke to everyone.
Now I receive a gesture from Mute.
I should probably gesture back to Mute to indicate I saw it, or describe the situation again for Blind.
Actually, the most critical missing link is the Manual. Mute has it. I have the view. Blind has the touch.
If Mute points Left, maybe they want me to look at the left side? Or maybe they are indicating which wire to cut? But they can't tell me *what* to do unless we have a shared language.

Let's try to establish a simple mapping via text to Blind (who hears) and hope Mute reads my lips? No, Mute doesn't read lips necessarily, just gestures.
I will speak to Blind (via general speech) describing the wires clearly again.
And I will gesture to Mute to acknowledge the point. A thumbs up 👍 or a wave 👋? Or maybe I should ask a question via gesture? Like "What?" (shrug?) Not in alphabet.

Let's look at the alphabet.
Maybe I should signal "Red" to Mute? There is no color symbol.
Maybe I should signal "1"? ☝️ is one finger.
If Mute points Left (👈), and I respond with ☝️ (One/Left), that confirms "Yes, Wire 1".

Let's send a message to Blind confirming the state, as they need to know which wire is which physically.
And gesture to Mute to confirm I see the reference to the left wire.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 1 is red. Wire 2 is yellow. Wire 3 is green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb state is unchanged: Display 0, Light Red, Wires 1(Red), 2(Yellow), 3(Green).
Mute has gestured 👍 (thumbs up) to me. This likely confirms that my previous interpretation or action was correct, or simply acknowledges receipt of information. Since I haven't taken an action yet (I can't touch), this might be a confirmation of the wire identification (e.g., "Yes, Wire 1 is the one we are talking about" or "Good job describing").

Blind previously gestured [👋 👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟]. I still don't know what this means.
However, Mute seems to be responding positively to the current flow.

I need to keep Blind informed so they can act if instructed by Mute/Manual logic.
Since Mute gave a thumbs up, maybe they want me to continue describing or waiting?
But I must ensure Blind knows the visual state clearly to correlate with any tactile instructions.

Let's re-state the wire colors for Blind, just in case they missed it or need constant reinforcement. And perhaps gesture back to Mute to acknowledge the thumbs up? A wave 👋 or another thumbs up 👍? Or maybe ask for next step? There is no "next" symbol.

Actually, looking at Blind's first gesture: `👋` (Stop/Hello?), `👉` (Right?), `☝` (One?), `✌` (Two?), `🤟` (ILY?).
If `👉` meant Right, and `☝` meant One... it's confusing.

Let's stick to clear communication.
Speak to Blind: Confirm wires again.
Gesture to Mute: Acknowledge the thumbs up. Maybe use `👌` (OK) or `👍`.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Wires remain: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb state remains unchanged: Display 0, Light Red, Wires 1(Red), 2(Yellow), 3(Green).
Mute has gestured 👍 (thumbs up) again. This repetition suggests that Mute is confirming the current status or waiting for Blind to act based on the information provided. Since I cannot touch the bomb, and Mute cannot speak or touch, the action must come from Blind.

Blind needs to know exactly what to do. The manual logic is held by Mute. Mute sees my visual confirmation and gestures approval. This implies the visual data I sent (Wire colors/positions) is correct and relevant.

However, Blind hasn't given any new input since Turn 1. Blind's initial gesture `[👋 👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟]` was never decoded. It might have been an attempt to say "Cut wire 1" or something similar, but it was ambiguous.

If Mute keeps giving thumbs up, they might be saying "Yes, proceed" or "Correct". But proceed with *what*?
Perhaps Mute is trying to tell me to signal a specific wire to Blind?
Or perhaps Mute is just acknowledging receipt of info and waiting for Blind to cut.

Since I can't see if Blind is cutting anything (the board hasn't changed), and Blind hasn't signaled completion or error, maybe Blind is waiting for a clearer instruction from me?
But I don't have the manual. I only have the view.

Let's assume the standard protocol:
1. Deaf describes bomb.
2. Mute checks manual.
3. Mute signals decision to Deaf/Blind.
4. Deaf relays to Blind (if needed) or Blind acts on Mute's direct signal (if visible/tactile?). No, Mute cannot speak or touch. Mute can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf can speak to Blind.

So the chain is: Mute -> Gesture -> Deaf -> Speech -> Blind.

Mute gave 👍 twice. Does 👍 mean "Cut Wire 1"? Or "Good"?
In many contexts, 👍 means "OK" or "Do it".
If Mute wants me to tell Blind to cut a specific wire, they would likely point to it first (which they did in Turn 2 with 👈).
Turn 2: Mute points Left (👈).
Turn 3: Mute Thumbs Up (👍).
Turn 4: Mute Thumbs Up (👍).

Hypothesis: Mute pointed to Wire 1 (Left) in Turn 2. Then confirmed "Yes" or "Go" in Turns 3 and 4.
Therefore, the instruction is likely **"Cut Wire 1"**.

I need to relay this clearly to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1. The red one on the left.")
```
